primary_paper.title: Dexamethasone and transdehydroandrosterone significantly reduce pulmonary epithelial cell injuries associated with mechanical ventilation

verified_figures.status: Visually checked original image matches the article's figure arrangement; show whole frame and source attribution.

rights: Owner was named author and prepared figures per article. Confirm publisher's reuse rights before public deployment. Film is a review-only draft.

scenes.heading: The interface was physical.
scenes.narration: This experiment began with an epithelial cell monolayer inside a parallel-plate chamber. The original paper documents the equipment, the moving interface, and how survival was assessed.

scenes.heading: A bubble crossed living cells.
scenes.narration: A single air bubble advanced over rat L2 alveolar epithelial cells. In this model, bubble travel was set at roughly three millimetres per second.

scenes.heading: The comparison was designed.
scenes.narration: Cells were examined without airflow injury and with bubble propagation. Other groups received dexamethasone, transdehydroandrosterone, or latrunculin A before exposure.

scenes.heading: Cell survival was measured.
scenes.narration: The study used a live-dead fluorescence assay. Calcein marked viable cells and ethidium homodimer identified damaged cells. Images were counted to estimate injury.

scenes.heading: The reported injury changed.
scenes.narration: Bubble exposure produced about fifty-five percent cell death. Pretreatment groups had lower reported death: approximately fifteen percent with dexamethasone and sixteen percent with DHEA.

scenes.heading: Cell mechanics offered a hypothesis.
scenes.narration: The authors examined actin organization and cellular morphology to explore why pretreatment could alter vulnerability. These measurements suggest mechanisms, but do not establish a patient-level effect.

scenes.heading: A chamber is not a human lung.
scenes.narration: The model used rat epithelial cells and a single bubble event. It does not reproduce all human ventilation conditions, systemic dosing, or clinical treatment outcomes.

scenes.heading: A result becomes a better question.
scenes.narration: What matters is the link between mechanics, cell properties, and injury under defined conditions. The next experiment must test how far that explanation actually travels.
